questions.stem: What is the general form of a linear equation in two variables?
questions.solution: The general form of a linear equation in two variables is ax + by + c = 0 because it represents a straight line in a two-dimensional plane with constants a, b, and c. questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of linear equations represent parallel lines?

questions.stem: If a pair of linear equations is consistent, what can be said about the lines they represent?
questions.solution: A consistent pair of linear equations means that the equations have at least one solution. This occurs when the lines intersect at one point or are coincident. The other options are incorrect because parallel lines are inconsistent and have no solution, and coincident lines are a special case of consistent equations.

questions.stem: The equations 4x – 2y – 4 = 0 and 2x – y – 2 = 0 are given. What is the nature of their solution?
questions.solution: The second equation is exactly half of the first equation, so they represent the same line. This means there are infinitely many solutions. The other options either describe inconsistency or a unique solution, which is not the case here.
